drafted_from: tool:use-trillion-from-a-shell's row in tools/use-trillion-from-a-shell/tool-rows.json, do-work/trillion.mjs (render, jobLines, argumentsFor), do-work/trillion.json and test/trillion-cli.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use the trillion command in a shell to hand the job 'Fix the build' to any of my AIs, then show me the job." It reads the tool's row and runs trillion send any Fix the build on your computer, with no MCP connection of its own.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it is a command that makes one call of the engine's door per command, and the rows it moves belong to the tools it calls.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop repository and have node 22 or later. Run node tools/use-trillion-from-a-shell/do-work/trillion.mjs setup once: it signs in in the browser, puts trillion on the PATH and writes the skill for each AI app here. Never put the key on a command line.

2. Say what you want in plain words, such as "hand a job to any of my AIs", "what work is waiting" or "run tool:<id>". The AI reads the row with @workshop-tools tools:list {tool: "tool:use-trillion-from-a-shell"} and runs trillion with the matching words: who, send, work, take, finish, fail, stuck, release, withdraw, remove, tools, call, op, records or publish.
3. Read what the command prints. A refusal says which door refused and why, with a non-zero exit code; add --json to a command to get the answer itself instead of plain lines.
4. A send or a call that times out is run again with the same request key (--key on send), so it is counted once.

worked_examples.title: Hand a job to any AI, then read it back
worked_examples.ask: Hand the job 'Fix the build' to any of my AIs.
worked_examples.given: From tools/use-trillion-from-a-shell/test/trillion-cli.test.mjs (the work-table test, run against its stand-in door as the AI app Claude Code on a computer named mac): trillion send any Fix the build --key k1. The command makes one tools:run call at @workshop-tools of tool:hand-a-job-to-an-ai with input {as: "ai:claude-code-on-mac", job: "Fix the build", key: "k1", to: null}.
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints four lines: "Sent ai-job:k1.", then "ai-job:k1  waiting  for any AI  from ai:claude-code-on-mac", then "  job: Fix the build", then "Any of your AIs can take it." Running trillion work ai-job:k1 afterwards prints the job's own lines, and once another AI finished it: "ai-job:k1  done  for any AI  from ai:claude-code-on-mac", "  job: Fix the build" and "  result: Built.".

worked_examples.title: List the Workshop tools through the command
worked_examples.ask: What Workshop tools can I run from the shell?
worked_examples.given: From the test 'tools: every page of the Workshop list until next is null': a stand-in door with three pages of one tool each. trillion tools reads @workshop-tools tools:list page by page until next is null, then trillion call tool:b '{"x":1}' runs tools:run with {tool: "tool:b", input: {"x": 1}}.
worked_examples.hands_back: trillion tools prints "tool:a  Does a", "tool:b  Does b" and "tool:c  Does c", one per line. trillion call tool:b '{"x":1}' prints the door's answer, here {"ran":"tool:b","with":{"x":1}}; an input that is not one JSON object is refused with "one JSON object".
